name: Jerry Carl
evidence: Former member (2021-25), returning after a gap; succeeds Barry Moore, who ran for Senate. Voted no on H.R. 8035 (April 2024 Ukraine aid) and yes on both Jan. 2021 objections to certifying AZ and PA electors; ran in 2026 on advancing Trump's 'America First' agenda. Won the Aug. 2026 special primary and the Nov. 3 general against Clyde Jones (D).

name: Shomari Figures
evidence: Not on the CPC roster; DW-NOMINATE (119th) -0.411, near the House Democratic median of -0.395. Called Israel an ally in 2024 and received a contribution from AIPAC PAC.

name: Mike Rogers
evidence: Voted yes on H.R. 8035 (2024 Ukraine aid) and no on the July 2025 Greene amendment to bar Ukraine funds; DW-NOMINATE 0.379 (46th most moderate of 227 Republicans). He did vote yes on both Jan. 2021 certification objections. Voted no on the June 2026 Ukraine Support Act (H.R. 2913), a discharge-petition bill opposed by 194 of 212 voting Republicans, so that vote is treated as weak evidence.

name: Amish Shah
evidence: Newcomer; flipped the seat Schweikert left to run for governor, defeating Jay Feely (R). His 2024 position paper backed continued U.S. aid to Israel with no 'additional restrictions'; he is described as a moderate. In the 2026 primary, PACs funded by AIPAC's United Democracy Project spent against him. No left economic program found.

name: Yassamin Ansari

key_endorsements: DMFI PAC (2024; she rejected its support in 2026)

evidence: Listed on the CPC roster and endorsed by CPC PAC; DW-NOMINATE -0.428 (85th most liberal of 222, moderately left of the median). Borderline on the Israel rule: DMFI backed her in 2024 as a 'pro-Israel progressive', but by 2026 she was rejecting DMFI support and had declined an AIPAC-linked Israel trip, citing Gaza.

name: Greg Stanton
evidence: Not on the CPC roster; DW-NOMINATE -0.281 (178th of 222, among the most moderate Democrats). Voted yes on H.R. 8034 (2024 Israel supplemental).

name: Mark Lamb
evidence: Newcomer (former Pinal County sheriff); succeeds Andy Biggs, who ran for governor, after defeating Elizabeth Lee (D). Ran on border enforcement and backing Trump's immigration crackdown; reported to have endorsed 'Great Replacement' framing on a QAnon-linked show (unverified allegation). No record on Ukraine.

name: JoAnna Mendoza
evidence: Newcomer; defeated incumbent Juan Ciscomani (R). Backed by Blue Dog PAC and NewDem Action Fund; affirmed support for Israel's security and a two-state solution (J Street, JDCA). Platform centers on cost of living.

name: Adelita Grijalva
evidence: Listed on the CPC roster; DW-NOMINATE -0.497 (32nd most liberal of 222). Cosponsored the Block the Bombs Act (H.R. 3565, which limits offensive arms to Israel) in her first week; sworn in Nov. 2025 after winning the special election.

name: Abraham Hamadeh
evidence: First term began 2025. Voted yes on the July 2025 Greene amendment to bar all Ukraine funds (76-341 overall); DW-NOMINATE 0.677 (186th of 227). Contested his 2022 Arizona attorney general loss in court. Voted no on the June 2026 Ukraine Support Act (H.R. 2913), a discharge-petition bill opposed by 194 of 212 voting Republicans, so that vote is treated as weak evidence.

name: Paul Gosar
evidence: Voted no on H.R. 8035 (2024 Ukraine aid), no on H.R. 8034, yes on the 2025 Greene amendment to bar Ukraine funds, and yes on both Jan. 2021 certification objections; DW-NOMINATE 0.701 (196th of 227).
